_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
"The container" is the messages container (".messages-container"), "the button" the scroll-to-bottom button (".scroll-to-bottom-button"), and "the gap" the container's scrollHeight - clientHeight - scrollTop. To "send" a message, fill the message input ([data-testid="message-input"]) with it and click the send button ([data-testid="send-button"]). Check every assertion with an eval that has "expect" (or an assert_* or wait_* step): an eval without "expect" asserts nothing. When a step says to record something, do it in one eval without "expect" that stores it in the named window variable, then check that variable. Perform the steps in order. The test seeds a conversation at /c/{{SLUG}} whose first message is "echo message 0". To "open the conversation", navigate to /c/{{SLUG}} and wait for the message input to be visible (allow 30s). To "add message N", send "echo message N" and wait until a [data-testid="message"] element containing the text "echo message N" is visible (allow 30s). A sub-margin scrollTop clamp does not strand the scroll-to-bottom button. The page provides window.__nudgeUp(): it lowers the container's scrollTop by 5, waits two animation frames, and resolves to the gap.
1. Open the conversation.
2. Enough content that the list actually scrolls: add message 1 and wait until the agent-thinking indicator ([data-testid="agent-thinking"]) is hidden (allow 30s); then add message 2 and wait until the agent-thinking indicator ([data-testid="agent-thinking"]) is hidden (allow 30s); then add message 3 and wait until the agent-thinking indicator ([data-testid="agent-thinking"]) is hidden (allow 30s).
3. Wait until Math.abs(gap) <= 1 is true. The button must not be visible (allow 5s).
4. Retry the nudge until it survives the bottom pin: eval (await window.__nudgeUp()) > 0 expecting true, allowing 15s (the eval runs again until it returns true).
5. The scroll event has been delivered by now, so this is a settled state: record in window.__buttonNow whether the button is visible right now (it exists, its getBoundingClientRect() has non-zero width and height, and its computed visibility is not "hidden"), in one eval without expect, then check that window.__buttonNow is false.
6. Send "echo after clamp" and wait until a [data-testid="message"] element containing "echo after clamp" is visible (allow 30s). The button must not be visible (allow 5s): still following.

steps.expression: const btn = document.querySelector('.scroll-to-bottom-button'); window.__buttonNow = !!(btn && btn.getBoundingClientRect().width > 0 && btn.getBoundingClientRect().height > 0 && window.getComputedStyle(btn).visibility !== 'hidden');
